newsitem.title: JAPAN: Malfunction causes western Japan reactor shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Malfunction causes western Japan reactor shutdown.

text.p: A nuclear reactor in western Fukui Prefecture shut down automatically on Monday morning, apparently due to an electrical failure, a Kansai Electric Power Co spokesman said.

The 1.18 million-kilowatt No. 4 reactor, located at Oi village, 370 km (230 miles) west of Tokyo, shut down after an alarm showed a malfunction in a generator and a main transformer, the spokesman said.
The exact cause of the trouble was under investigation, but the reactor and the cooling system were not affected and no radiation was released outside the reactor, he said.
The shutdown was the first at the plant since the reactor started commercial operation in February 1993, he said.
